solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Approve draughtsman's items used by most of Florida city

parts.note: rubbers are erasers, kept by a draughtsman for correcting drawings

indicators.note: only most of the city name is used, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: Tampa is a city on Florida's west coast

explanation.surface: Someone approves the tools used by a draughtsman working in a Florida city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last A of TAMPA, leaving TAMP. 'Rubbers' is the British word for erasers.
explanation.definitionFit: To give official but unthinking approval is to put an official stamp on something without real scrutiny.

clue.text: Quell resistance by English journalists

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
the press is the body of journalists

explanation.surface: An English newspaper crowd puts down an uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to hold down or subdue, as with a revolt or a feeling.

clue.text: Note always heading to bathroom to when getting up

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the letters rise, so they are read from bottom to top

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter, so bathroom gives its opening letter

explanation.surface: A reminder to always head to the bathroom on getting up in the morning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when getting up' turns EVER + B round to give the answer. The two 'to's are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A breve is a musical note lasting twice as long as a semibreve.

clue.text: Former queen blocks acclaim for government department

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: the queen's letters sit inside the acclaim word and obstruct it

parts.note: a cheer is a shout of acclaim

explanation.surface: A former queen stands in the way of praise for a Whitehall department.
explanation.definitionFit: The Exchequer is the UK government department in charge of public revenue, headed by the Chancellor.

clue.text: Victory, perhaps, and second with it

parts.note: hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A victory, perhaps, and coming second while being trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Victory, Nelson's flagship at Trafalgar, is the example: 'perhaps' marks it as one instance.
explanation.definitionFit: HMS Victory is a famous naval vessel, so it is one example of a seagoing vessel.

clue.text: Extraordinary run from paralytic drunk

indicators.note: drunk suggests the letters of paralytic are reeling into a new order

parts.note: r is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone describes an unusual run by a heavily intoxicated person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' says R is taken away: rearrange PARALYTIC without its R. 'Paralytic' is British slang for very drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unusual or out of the ordinary does not fit the typical pattern.

clue.text: Boss regularly cracks a Toughie?

indicators.note: the regular letters break into the middle of the other word

parts.note: per means a, as in 'ten pounds a head'

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of boss

explanation.surface: The puzzle editor regularly solves a hard crossword.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital T on 'Toughie' suggests the Telegraph puzzle series, but here it is just a hard question.
explanation.definitionFit: A difficult problem or question is a teaser that is tough to answer.

clue.text: Location that could make e.g. egress?

parts.note: split as an instruction, the solution says tack four letters onto e.g., which turns it into egress

explanation.surface: A spot that might, for example, serve as a way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer into two words: an instruction to tack RESS onto 'e.g.', which spells 'egress'. 'that could make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A street number and name tell you where someone lives, so it pinpoints a place.

clue.text: Soup in summer month? That's about right

indicators.note: the month goes about, or around, the right

parts.note: June is a summer month in the northern hemisphere
a lien is a legal right to hold property until a debt is paid

explanation.surface: A soup eaten in a summer month seems roughly correct.
explanation.definitionFit: A clear broth containing thin strips of vegetables is called a julienne soup.

clue.text: Go on at length and pacify her rages

indicators.note: letters that rage run wild, so the words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone rants on and tries to calm a woman who is furious.
explanation.definitionFit: To moralise tediously and at length is to sermonise in a tiresome way.

clue.text: Group agreed to skip about

indicators.note: skipping the letters for about leaves them out

parts.note: squared means settled or agreed, as in squaring it with the boss
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A group consent to jumping around.
explanation.definitionFit: A squad is a small team or group of people, such as soldiers or players.

clue.text: Number to the left?

parts.note: look to the left of the clue: the figure printed there is the clue number, 11

explanation.walkthrough: The clue points to its own printed clue number, which sits to its left on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: The clue number printed beside this clue is 11, the figure spelt out as the answer.

clue.text: Fighter plane heading east to take in bad weather — it's a pain

indicators.note: the plane and compass point together take the weather inside them

parts.note: the MiG is a Soviet-designed fighter aircraft
rain counts as bad weather

explanation.surface: A jet heads east into rain, which is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' is a link word between plane and direction.
explanation.definitionFit: A severe recurring headache is a pain in the head, so the definition fits loosely.

clue.text: Figure in flap involving university

indicators.note: involving means surrounding, so the panic word wraps around the letter

parts.note: a state is a flap or panic, as in getting into a state

explanation.surface: A figure is caught up in a panic about the university.
explanation.definitionFit: A sculpted representation of a person is a figure in stone or bronze.

clue.text: In temper, promoted detectives stand down

indicators.note: the turned-round detectives go in the temper word

parts.note: to abate is to moderate or temper

indicators.note: in a down clue, promoted means moved upward, so the letters are read bottom to top

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the detective branch of British police

explanation.surface: Angry detectives, recently promoted, resign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In temper' poses as 'angry', but 'temper' is the verb meaning to moderate. CID is the British police detective branch.
explanation.definitionFit: A monarch who gives up the throne is said to step aside or resign the role.

clue.text: Police leader has arrests for Sussex town

indicators.note: arrests means holds, so the clue word has keeps the singer inside it

parts.note: Sting was the frontman of the rock band The Police

explanation.surface: A police chief makes arrests in a seaside town.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital P of 'Police' at the start of the clue hides the band The Police.
explanation.definitionFit: This East Sussex seaside town is where the famous battle of 1066 is named after.

clue.text: Bite before swallowing skin of Indian fruit

parts.note: tang is a sharp taste, a bite

indicators.note: the old word for before takes the outer letters inside it

parts.note: ere is an old word for before

indicators.note: the skin of a word is its outer letters

explanation.surface: Bite into the peel of an Indian fruit before swallowing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus fruit like a mandarin orange.

clue.text: Leaves describing Republican that is on the payroll

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the leaves surround the other letters

parts.note: a salad is a dish of leaves
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Someone resigns after describing a Republican who's on staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb (quits) but is a noun for salad leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker paid a fixed regular wage by an employer is on its payroll.

clue.text: Official chap with less on top? Not at first

indicators.note: the first letter is left off

parts.note: someone with less hair on top is balder
man means chap

explanation.surface: A council official is a fellow who is losing his hair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with less on top' is a playful way of describing a man going bald; the pieces go in answer order, not clue order.
explanation.definitionFit: An alderman is a senior elected member of a borough or county council, a civic official.

clue.text: Liberal exposed rich supporting terribly racy material

indicators.note: in a down clue, a supporting piece sits below the one it holds up
terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled
exposed means stripped of its outer letters

explanation.surface: A liberal-minded person exposes a rich backer of very racy material.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, a piece 'supporting' another sits below it, so the scrambled 'racy' comes first.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrylic is a synthetic fibre or fabric, so it is a type of cloth.

clue.text: Scoff as a joke is delivered

indicators.note: a line delivered is spoken, so the sound of the phrase counts

parts.note: in jest means as a joke

explanation.surface: Someone mocks something said in fun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scoff' looks like mockery but is the British slang sense of eating greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To scoff food is to eat it, which means taking it into the body.

clue.text: Communist sent up to inspire soldiers in distress

indicators.note: to inspire is to breathe in, so the reversed word takes in the soldiers
in a down clue, sent up means the letters are reversed upward

parts.note: Trot is short for Trotskyist, a type of communist
men means soldiers, as in officers and men

explanation.surface: A communist is sent up to rally troops in trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe suffering, physical or mental, is anguish or distress.

clue.text: Stack small fruit in vehicle

parts.note: a rick is a stack of hay
a haw is the fruit of the hawthorn

explanation.surface: A pile of small fruit sits inside a cart.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled passenger cart pulled or pedalled by one person.

clue.text: Cake finally rises once cooked

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of rises
cooked means the word once is reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cake at last rises once it is baked.
explanation.definitionFit: A scone is a small British baked item, a kind of plain cake eaten with jam and cream.

clue.text: Bloke's spring broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put on air, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: a geyser is a hot spring

explanation.surface: A man's leap is aired on the radio.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is a link (bloke is). The two sound alike in British speech. Geezer is British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal British words for a man or fellow.

clue.text: Country, once unknown, almost made known

parts.note: z is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: aired means made known, as with views

explanation.surface: A country that was once obscure has nearly come to light.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the name of the Democratic Republic of the Congo from 1971 to 1997, a former country name.

clue.text: Beautiful, fine tune

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A lovely, excellent melody.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair is an old poetic word for lovely, as in 'fair maiden'.

clue.text: Release building blocks? About time!

indicators.note: about means around, so the toy bricks surround the letter

parts.note: Lego is the toy brand of plastic building blocks

explanation.surface: A child is told to hand back the toy bricks at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About time!' reads as impatience but 'About' means round T.
explanation.definitionFit: To release something is to stop holding it, to loosen your grip.

clue.text: Appeal is penned by girl to make text stand out

parts.note: it means sex appeal, as in 'she's got it'

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the girl's name holds the other word inside

parts.note: Alice is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl writes a plea to have her text highlighted.
explanation.definitionFit: Setting words in slanted type is a way of giving emphasis on the page.

clue.text: Backing European people to settle in northern county

indicators.note: the people settle in, going inside the county letters

parts.note: Dorset is a county on England's south coast
men means people

explanation.surface: Support for Europeans moving into a county in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northern county' looks like one county in the north, but it is N plus DORSET, a southern English county.
explanation.definitionFit: An endorsement is approval or support given to a person or product.
